HxResult HxWindowDelete ( HxWindow_t *  pWindow  ) 

Deallocate a window.

HxWindowDelete deletes the window. This also deletes all of the widgets that are in the window, descending down through the whole widget hierarchy.

You cannot delete the application window. Passing the app window or NULL to this wwill return HX_INVALID_ARG and do nothing. The application window will be deleted by the system when you call HxUiRelease at the end of your program.

Parameters:
hWindow IN: Handle to window to be deleted
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success. Returns HX_INVALID_ARG if passed the application window.

HxResult HxWindowEventLoop ( HxWindow_t *  pWindow,
int32_t  timeout 
)

Enter the main event loop.

HxWindowEventLoop is called by the application after the application set-up is complete, and the application is ready to process input events.

The timeout argument is used by the system to determine how long to remain in the event loop. After that many milliseconds, the event loop will end as soon as there are no pending input events.

The application's thread blocks until the next event occurs, or until the timeout occurs. A timeout value of 0 waits forever for events. If the timeout triggers, HX_TIMEOUT is returned. HX_INTERRUPTED is returned if the blocking action is interrupted due to a threading error.

Parameters:
pWindow IN: Pointer to a window, or NULL for AppWindow
timeout IN: Timeout value, or 0 for no timeout
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if event loop exited by a call to HxWindowExitEventLoop. Returns HX_TIMEOUT if timeout triggers. Returns HX_DESTROYED if pWindow is closed.

HxResult HxWindowExitEventLoop ( void   ) 

HxResult HxWindowFlushRepeatEvents ( DFBWindowEvent *  pEvent  ) 

Flush repeated events from the queue.

HxWindowFlushRepeatEvents is used to remove any events from the top of the queue that repeat the event passed in as pEvent. For example, passing a key down event would flush out repeat events for the same key, but not for other keys. This is used at the end of an event handler to avoid having an overflow of input events when your handler may not finish before another event arrives.

Parameters:
pEvent IN: Pointer to the "prototype" event used to determine what to flush from the queue.

HxResult HxWindowGetWindowByIndex ( uint32_t  index,
HxWindow_t **  hWindow,
HxWindowType_t *  pType 
)

Return the next visible window.

HxWindowGetWindowByIndex returns the next visible window, beginning with the topmost window (index 0).

The total of visible windows is returned by HxWindowGetCount. HxWindowGetWindowByIndex can be called with an index of 0 through (count - 1), with the bottom window being the application window.

The pType argument returns the window type. It can be set to NULL if the caller does not care.

If an error occurs, *hWindow is set to NULL, and *pType is set to kHxWindowInvalid.

Parameters:
index IN: Index into visible windows
hWindow OUT: Pointer to window pointer
index OUT: Pointer to window type, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success. Returns HX_NOT_FOUND if window index not found.

HxResult HxWindowGrabScrollEvents ( HxWindow_t *  pWindow,
HxWidget_t *  pWidget 
)

Set receiver for scroll events.

HxWindowGrabScrollEvents specifies a widget that should receive all scroll wheel and up/down arrow key events sent to the window, regardless of which widget has focus.

This API is typically used by dialogs that contains a dominant list and several command buttons (like the file dialogs). By sending all scroll events to the list, the user can easily scroll through the list without having to navigate to it.

Only one widget can grab scroll events. If this function is called more than once for the same window, the last widget grabs the events.

If pWidget is set to NULL, then no widget grabs the events for the window.

If the grabbing widget is disabled or set invisible, then scroll events are handled normally.

The implementation of tab widgets (see hxtabs.h) hides and shows containers in response to the user selecting the tab buttons. If the container has a child list that grabs scroll events, the application should listen for the kHxTabsSelected message so that the list can release or grab scroll events as its parent container is shown or hidden.

Parameters:
pWindow IN: Pointer to a window, or NULL for AppWindow
pWidget IN: Pointer to widget, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxWindowLockSurface ( HxWindow_t *  pWindow,
void **  hDstBuf,
int32_t *  pPitch 
)

Lock the display, and get a pointer to its data.

HxWindowLockSurface is the accessor to the data pointer for the frame buffer associated with a window.

In order to get the pointer to the frame buffer, the frame buffer must be locked down. This prevents other threads from trying to draw to the frame buffer at the same time. While holding this lock, no other drawing can occur. Any attempt to draw will not cause an error, but the new data will be ignored and not transferred to the display, even when the surface is later unlocked.

Consequently, the application must be very careful when using this API. Every call to HxWindowLockSurface must have a matching call to HxWindowUnlockSurface. And care must be taken during the locked phase: the application should not allow the event loop to run, which could cause a screen update to get lost.

In addtion to a pointer to the frame buffer, this function returns the pitch, or bytes per row, of the frame buffer if pPitch is not NULL.

Parameters:
pWindow IN: Pointer to a window, or NULL for AppWindow
hDstBuf OUT: Handle to the window's frame buffer
pPitch OUT: Pointer to the frame buffer pitch, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success.

HxWindowNew allocates a new onscreen window. The window is created using kHxWindowAttrDefault.

hWindow OUT: Handle to window
Returns:

HxResult HxWindowSetFocusArray ( HxWindow_t *  pWindow,
const uint32_t *  pIdArray,
int32_t  idCount 
)

Change the widget focus order for a window.

HxWindowSetFocusArray allows the application to change the focus order of the widgets contained within a window. This function should be called before calling HxWindowEventLoop.

By default, the focus order of widgets is by order of creation.

The ID array should normally contain all of the widget ID's in the window. If an invalid ID is passed into the array, no error is returned, but any missing widgets will no longer be capable of receiving focus for purposes of keyboard navigation.

Passing an idCount of 0 disables the toolkit's handling of keyboard navigation for the window. If idCount is 0, then pIdArray can be NULL.

If widgets are allocated after this function is called, the new widgets are appended to the focus array.

Parameters:
pWindow IN: Pointer to a window (or NULL for app window)
pIdArray IN: Array of widget ID's
idCount IN: Size of the widget ID array
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK if successful.

HxResult HxWindowSetHandler ( HxWindow_t *  pWindow,
HxHandlerSelector_t  selector,
HxWindowEventFunc  pCallback,
void *  pData,
HxWindowEventFunc *  hOldCallback,
void **  hOldData 
)

Set a window input event handler.

HxWindowSetHandler is available to applications that need to customize the processing of input events for a window.

Applications that override the default handler should save the default handler before replacing it with a custom handler, and restore it when appropriate. The application's handler should call the default handler before exiting to ensure that system behavior (i.e., focus navigation using the tab key, detection of double and triple button click, scroll wheel acceleration) is preserved.

If the custom key and mouse button handler returns HX_OK, the system then calls the widget's key and mouse button callbacks. If the application does not want the widget callbacks called, the custom handler must return HX_EVENT_HANDLED.

If pCallback is NULL, the default callback and data is restored. hOldCallback and hOldData are ignored if set to NULL.

Warning: menus and drop-down boxes use mouse button handlers. Applications should not replace their handlers while they are open.

Parameters:
pWindow IN: Pointer to window, or NULL for AppWindow
selector IN: Selector for type of event handler
pCallback IN: Pointer to the new HxWindowEventFunc, or NULL
pData IN: User data, or NULL
hOldCallback OUT: Handle to the old callback, or NULL
hOldData OUT: Handle to the old user data, or NULL
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success.

HxResult HxWindowSetOpacity ( HxWindow_t *  pWindow,
uint8_t  opacity 
)

Set the opacity of a window.

HxWindowSetOpacity sets the opacity of a window. The opacity argument is an 8 bit unsigned value. A value of 0xFF sets the window to be fully opaque, a value of 0 causes the window to be invisible. Intermediate values cause varying degrees of window transparancy.

Parameters:
pWindow IN: Pointer to a window, or NULL for AppWindow
opacity IN: A value from 0 (invisible) to 0xFF (opaque)
Returns:
HxResult: Returns HX_OK on success.

Unlock the display.

HxWindowUnlockSurface unlocks a surface that was locked due to a prior call to HxWindowLockSurface.
